title: SQL compilation artifact (fixture expected/ shape)
description: Deliberately lightweight: this catches gross authoring mistakes in a hand-written expected artifact. It does not validate the SQL text itself, only the artifact's outer shape (AR-4: parameterized SQL text + ordered/named parameter list); since #1638 a SQL compiler (Craticula.Sql) checks the rest semantically, by compiling every in-scope artifact and comparing it byte for byte -- across all five dialects since #1642. The wording here said 'no SQL compiler exists yet to check these semantically, per #1630's context.md' until #1643's review pass, which found it still standing beside its already-repaired Mongo counterpart.

dialect.description: Which SQL dialect this artifact targets. Four are v1-supported (§5); 'oracle' was added in #1642 and is COMMUNITY-TESTED — it is graded by this artifact suite exactly like the other four and, since #2880, also run against a real Oracle Database Free 23ai in the execution tier; that tier is not part of the pull-request gate, the release workflow does run it (a failing Oracle test stops a release), and Oracle 12.2 to 21c were not run (OQ-6 is closed on that footing). See spec/fixtures/README.md's support tiering.

sql.description: The parameterized SQL text. Must never contain a literal user value inlined as text (SEC-2) — only identifiers/keywords and parameter placeholders.

params.description: Ordered parameter values, one per placeholder in 'sql', in the placeholder's positional/named order. Each entry is the literal driver-bound value, not a tagged typedValue — by this stage the value has left the IR and become a query parameter. Usually a JSON string/number/boolean/null, but ALSO legitimately an array: SQL-4 (spec/semantics.md) binds a Postgres set membership as ONE array parameter ('"status" = ANY($1)' with params [["active","pending"]]), where dialects rendering 'IN (...)' bind N scalars instead. A decimal is a numeric STRING, never a JSON number (AR-7) — it and a double are otherwise the same wire shape. 'items: {}' is therefore deliberate: no per-entry validation here, because only the field's declared type distinguishes the legal shapes.
